en: ...No Raza, Ober, or Phantom\nships in the vicinity... We're\nfinally in a safe zone.

...But the shock from the Silvarant's
sinking has messed up the rear reactor
readings. Coro, can you do something
about it from the inside?

We have no idea what might happen in
this sector. For our safety, we should
hide in this asteroid belt for a while and
focus on repairs.
How long will it take?

Even for a single sensor,
depending on the extent of the
damage, it will take at least
half a day...

Half a day... Dammit! Lover, can't you
get a hold of Isabel somehow?! That
bastard Asmodeus, if he gives the
Phantom ship to Isabel...!
Heath!

Neither the Overman nor our comrades are in
any condition to fly into a battlefield right now.
Even this asteroid belt is within Ober's airspace.
Any careless communication will just draw the
enemy to us.
...Dammit!

...Administrator Koro. Please hurry the
repairs as much as possible. At this
point, I doubt the Silvarant was actually
the flagship, but...

I can't imagine the Ober army would
just ignore the sinking of such a
massive vessel. Their search will
eventually reach this area.
Agreed. Everyone who is free,\nlet's hurry up and repair the\nship.
...Boss...

I don't even know where to
start. Once the ship is fixed,
should we first check if Isabel
is safe?
I'm not sure. With Givel in this\nstate, I feel like it'll be\ndangerous wherever we go.

Whether he's awake or asleep,
he's nothing but a nuisance. If
it weren't for Eve, I'd want to
finish him off right now.

Don't be ridiculous... I went
through the humiliation of such
a spectacle... just to recover
him.

...While he's still alive, I must
use every bone, every strand
of hair... as experimental
material...
I'd really prefer it if you didn't\nsay such dangerous things...

It doesn't sound like a joke to
me. With this guy, you can't
feel safe no matter how much
you restrain him.
There's no guarantee he's as\nweakened as he looks.
I'm on edge just thinking about\nwhether he'll wake up first or\nthe ship will be fixed first.
But it's true that he was restrained by\nAsmodeus. Maybe his wounds from the\nbattle in the Gap haven't healed yet?
Even after all these months?
For now, our only option is to\nkeep a constant watch with\nseveral people.
Verda?
Everyone else is working\ntogether to repair and inspect\nthe ship.

We must return the ship to full working
order and descend to a planet with an
atmosphere as soon as possible,
otherwise we'll be helpless when Givel
wakes up.
...That's not important. More\nimportantly, how did it go?

Ah, I was able to collect plenty of
samples even amidst all that
commotion. A full flask's worth―the one
the Captain bought for me previously.
This here is the surplus.
The liquid that filled the\ncapsule Givel was in.

Between Givel, that Phantom of
unknown origin, and the way
Asmodeus was manipulating
Eve...
There were plenty of hints.\nIdentifying the components was\nsimple.
Even I can tell if you put it that\nway. It was all sparkly and\nrainbow-colored.
It's Gems, right?

Indeed. It is a refined version of the
Gems collected from the Azurite
system. Ideally, I would have liked to
examine the machine itself, but...
However, if Givel was immersed\nin high-purity liquid Gems...
That means Givel is the source\nof most of the Phantoms\naround here.

It is highly likely. Asmodeus
mentioned it as well. This
liquid... let us call it "Emblem
Water" for now.

There were traces of a special
emblem that I, as a layman,
cannot identify. I would like to
leave this analysis to Mastima.
Once I have recovered a bit\nmore...
Alright. Looks like we've\nreached a conclusion, so shall\nwe finish them off?
Wait, wait, wait, Welch! It's too\nsoon!
Why?!
Because we still don't know\nwhy Eve was trying to protect\nGivel.
Can't we just pry that out of\nthem after we finish them off?
...Eve was so stubborn about it.\nIf we kill Givel now, Eve might\nnever come back to us.
...Good grief, what on earth is\nEve thinking...
One thing is for sure: Eve is\ndefinitely not on friendly terms\nwith Asmodeus.
I'm certain she has no intention\nof siding with Ober or running\nwild using the Phantom.

But if that's the case, wouldn't
it have made sense for her to
return to us once Mastima
secured Givel?

That be the most confusing part. I
suppose we must assume there was
some reason other than Givel that kept
her bound to Asmodeus.
It seems our next move should\nwait until Givel wakes up.

At the very least, Givel must have some
kind of connection to Asmodeus, and
he was obsessed with Eve's existence
from the start...

I think our only option is to get
the truth about the relationship
between Asmodeus and Eve
from Givel.
Even if he wakes up, I doubt\nhe'll talk willingly...
Just when I thought we were\nmaking progress, we hit a dead\nend.

If this is how it's going to be, it
would be much easier if Givel
were just pulling all the strings
from the shadows.

Back during the Holy War, I used to
think how much easier the world would
be if everything ended just by
defeating one villain hiding somewhere...
Hm?
Big brother Euwin. How's Givel\ndoing?
As you can see. What's wrong,\nTika?
Hmm, how do I put this... it's\nkind of like I have some good\nnews and some bad news.
What is that supposed to\nmean?
Well, about Isabel... it looks like\nshe really did sink.
H-how can you say something\nlike that so casually!

But Captain Jeanne, Kevin, and all the
other crew members managed to
escape safely. I received an encrypted
transmission from Captain Jeanne
herself.

I-is that so? Well, that is
certainly good news, but you're
really jumping all over the
place!
Asmodeus mentioned sending\nthe Phantom ships after them.\nDid they repel the attack?

No, the Phantom ships that
were pursuing them suddenly
vanished, and the attack
stopped.
That gave them enough time\nbefore the ship sank to get\neveryone out.
Damned nerve, giving us a\nscare like that.

The boss, Kevin, and a few others
escaped in the same lifeboat and were
apparently picked up by the security
forces at Stardust Bazaar.
But they still don't know what\nhappened to the rest of the\ncrew.

Warp with a lifeboat? No way.
If we could do that, we
wouldn't have needed your help
in the first place.
Raza hasn't been able to shrink\nwarp drives down to that size.

Once you're in a lifeboat, you just land
on the nearest safe planet, send out a
distress signal, and wait for a Raza ship
to find you.
In that sense, it's a miracle we\neven made it into the Bazaar's\nterritory.

Speaking of miracles, what's
the deal with the Phantom ship
that was chasing us suddenly
vanishing?
Those guys aren't the type to\njust change targets for our\nconvenience.
If Givel was involved in the\nPhantoms' appearance,
then perhaps Mastima's crest\nmagic, which freed Givel from\nthe machine, had an effect.

So in the end, the source of the
Phantom outbreaks wasn't Grigori, but
Givel. I'm not sure if that's something to
be relieved about.

With a dangerous guy like that
on board, we can't exactly
head out in the Overman to
rescue the bosses right now.
Lover. How much longer until\nthe repairs are finished?

Everyone's helping, so it should
be faster than expected, but
it'll still take another three
hours.
Coro. Shouldn't Rekoro be able\nto pinpoint the location of\nIsabel's crew?
I thought so too, so I'm trying\nto get in touch with Rekoro\nnow.

It seems Rekoro is currently
calculating to distinguish the
lifeboats from the wreckage of
the Isabel... Huh?
...Excuse me?
Givel has woken up.
Eek!? I-I-Is he okay?
Yeah. He's not acting out; he's\nbeing quiet.

He says he wants to talk to
the Captain and Karlyn. If
anyone else is free, could you
come over?

There is no need to be so guarded.
What could you possibly fear from
someone who has suffered the plight of
a prisoner and remains bound?

...Didn't you say you had something to
discuss with the Captain and me? If
you have no intention of speaking
properly, I'll kill you right here and now.
Heh heh heh... You've certainly\ngrown bold... ugh...
...I do not mind. Do as you wish,\nKarlyn Kayson. You have every\nreason and right to do so.

Stop with the cheap provocations. And
Karlyn, don't take the bait. We all know
the situation has changed since we last
met.

...You wonder why I am in a place like
this? I was defeated by you all and
cast out from the Rift; this was simply
the universe I returned to.

In this sector, many Gems are
crowded together due to the
influence of the Urza Gate's
crest power.
...Though none of them were\nfully responsive to my power...
The Urza Gate...? Do you mean\nthe Urza System?
What does that mean? What\ndo you know about the Urza\nSystem?
...I did not call you here to\nanswer your questions.

I had you summoned because I
have something to ask you, as
the Captain of the ship
carrying Evelysse.
So condescending... I'm\nseriously tempted to just kill\nhim.

Answer me truthfully. Where...
did you meet Evelysse? It
could not have been in the
Daft system.
Um, that planet, right? Now\nthat I think about it, it didn't\nreally have a name...?
...Where?

It's hard to explain exactly
where... but it's about 100
light-years away from the
Azurite system.
It wasn't a star system with an\nadvanced civilization, so it\ndidn't have a name.

The coordinates on the star
map follow our technology, so I
don't think telling you verbally
will help.
...Was there a blue planet\nnearby?
A blue planet? You mean a\nstar?
A planet. A blue planet where\nHumans survive, with abundant\nwater and atmosphere...?
Oh, yes, there was! A lush\nplanet with 60% ocean\ncoverage!
But that planet was also an\nundeveloped world, so we just\ncalled it "Planet Maere."
...Whether it's a coincidence or\na misunderstanding, I suppose\nthings remain the same...

...Now then, Givel. Ever since you first
saw Eve at Baschen's imperial castle,
you've been strangely obsessed with
getting your hands on her.

It seems you knew from the very start
that Eve possessed a Summoning
Crest. You even mentioned that you'd
been searching for her for a long time,
didn't you?
Do you know something about\nEve's past? Just what exactly\nis your relationship with her?
...That's enough. I'm going to\nsleep.

Hey...! What's with that
attitude?! You're a prisoner
right now, do you even know
your place?!

If you're that sleepy, maybe
Welch-chan should give you a
taste of her special wake-up
hammer?! Huh?!
...Welch, go ahead and do as\nyou say.
What?!
He won't bare his fangs at us\nanymore.

He could call as many Phantoms as he
wanted if he wished, yet he shows no
sign of doing so. He's not the type to
fight a losing battle.
Karlyn! This!
...Huh? What is it?
A hammer. I'll lend it to you, so\nif anything happens, give 'em a\ngood old-fashioned wallop!
...Thanks, I'll take it. "Punch\nyour way to a severance\npackage," was it?
Just make sure you don't have\nany regrets.
Thank you. And Henri, I'm sorry.\nI think I've lost my cool a bit.

It cannot be helped. Your situation is
unique, Karlyn. If keeping watch
becomes too much, don't push yourself;
take a rest.
I appreciate it.

Ugh! Bad people really have it easy,
don't they?! They get to eat and sleep
whenever they want, and they can just
play dumb whenever things get
inconvenient!
I wouldn't want to be like that\nmyself.
...What do we do now?

Since we have no lead on Eve's
whereabouts, we have no choice but to
start with what we can reach. For now,
we shall investigate the data gathered
by the Silvarant.

We cannot simply leave Givel
be, so Valka has been handling
most of the internal records on
her own...

What about regrouping with
Captain Jeanne and Kevin?
Thanks to Rekoro, we have
located their evacuation point.
We can do that after we finish\nchecking the Silvarant's data.
Heath, are you sure about\nthis?

If we know they're safe, they'll
just give us grief if we go see
them before finishing what
needs to be done.
Besides, I've stumbled upon\nsomething rather interesting.

<font color=blue>Heath</font> We've tracked various
Phantom traces on our way
here. While doing that, a few
things caught my eye...

You remember that secret
code Valka found, sent from
Ober's space station toward
Raza?

And Verda, you mentioned that
the liquid Givel was submerged
in was made from processed
Gems, right?
<font color=blue>Verda</font> That is correct, but...
<font color=blue>Heath</font> The final party in\nLover's dealings was McKinley\nof the Raza army.

And then there's Lazuli, which Raza and
Ober are fighting over despite it having
no resources, but instead possessing
that Urza System thing that runs on
Gems.
<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> ...What's wrong? Why\nare you suddenly getting so\nserious?

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Right. Keeping all that in mind,
take a look at this. These are the
records of cargo brought into Silvarant
over the last few months.
<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> ...Wait. This container\nbelongs to the Rose family...

<font color=blue>Verda</font> Does this mean one of
the trading partners from back
then leaked Gems to the Ober
army?

<font color=blue>Heath</font> No. I found something
strange when I traced the
history of this container. Look
at the contents.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> Huh? These stones are dull. We
should have handed over the ones we
collected for this deal, so they should
be much prettier...

<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> ...You mean these are
Gems my family traded before
we ever met the Captain and
the others?

<font color=blue>Heath</font> Exactly. Moreover, the tag
records that this container was
originally transported to a Raza army
ship that the Rose family had been
dealing with.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> What?!

<font color=blue>Lavarnia</font> ...The stones we were
supposed to have sold to the Raza
army ended up in Silvarant, where the
Givel that creates Phantoms was held?
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Well? Don't you think\nthis is a pretty interesting\nstory?

<font color=blue>Verda</font> Indeed... Two sides that
are supposed to be at war,
exchanging supplies right on
the front lines...

And Gems that can be used in
the Urza System, which are
kept secret even from Raza's
own soldiers...
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Normally, you'd just\nthink it was a simple case of a\nspy infiltrating the ranks.

But I already know that Gems aren't
just resources. They're something that
could be used for something absolutely
staggering.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Givel was a prisoner of\nthe Ober army.

The time Asmodeus became the
Commander-in-Chief of the Ober army
coincides with when the Phantoms
began to appear...
Could it be that Raza's army\nknew Ober was going to start\ndeploying Phantoms?

<font color=blue>Heath</font> If that's the case, then
McKinley's strange behavior when he
tried to steal the Gems from us
suddenly makes a lot of sense.

It would mean that Raza and Ober,
despite being at war, were actually
colluding under the cover of the
fighting on the front lines.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> Mista Heath's hypothesis\nis spot on.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Valka.

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Please look at this. In addition to
the space bases, I discovered
encrypted communications addressed
to Raza within the Silvarant.
As I mentioned before, the\nRaza word for Phantom\nappears frequently within them.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Right. ...And?

<font color=blue>Valka</font> Just three days after the
Phantom fleet appeared before the
Raza army, a massive amount of
encrypted communication was sent
from the Raza home planet.

Surprisingly, the majority of the content
consisted of the Raza army's advance
plans. The Raza high command was
leaking operational secrets to the
enemy.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> What... the hell is that?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> This is an even bigger\nproblem.

It's essentially a secret ledger. The
trade of Gems between the Raza
front-line units and the Ober army
dates back at least ten years.
<font color=blue>Heath</font> Whoa, whoa, whoa...

<font color=blue>Valka</font> A vast quantity of Gems were
traded during this time, but strangely,
the volume dropped sharply around the
time Commander-in-Chief Asmodeus
took office.

And it seems the trade was
scheduled to end with the final
shipment McKinley was
planning to bring in.

On the surface, it looks as though
Commander-in-Chief Asmodeus carried
out a reform to dismantle the corrupt
system of collusion with the enemy
upon establishing his new regime.
But we know that he is not\nthat kind of person.
So I looked into it further and\nfound this image file.
A photo of the Silvarant's\nouter hull?

It's the plate showing the ship's name.
Can you see the small, different
characters engraved on the bottom
right of this plate?
...What is this? It looks like the\nOber language...
This image was stored in the\noldest part of the Silvarant's\nvideo archives.
Based on various data, it is\nestimated that the ship was\nbuilt nearly 30 years ago.
With that in mind, look at this\nphrasing. In the language of\nOber, it says this:
Come, Asmodeus. Our great\nleader.
30 years ago? You mean\nbefore the war even started?
It feels less like praising a\nleader and more like a prayer\nto a god.

Dr. Belda's intuition is correct. It is
presumed that to some of the people
of Ober, Asmodeus was a being
equivalent to a mythological god.

I found numerous standard
reports that end with a closing
prayer for something called
"the protection of Asmodeus."

Then is it possible that the Asmodeus
who appeared before everyone isn't
actually the Demon Lord the Captain
mentioned,

but just some Ober citizen
pretending to be Asmodeus to
take advantage of the people's
faith?
...No, I doubt it. It seems we'll\nneed to ask Welch to wake\nGivel up.

Indeed. If he were just an ordinary Ober
citizen claiming to be Asmodeus, there
would be no reason why he could
capture Givel and manipulate Eve.
Besides, isn't Asmodeus recorded in\nthe Galactic Federation as the Demon\nLord who plunged planets into terror?

Considering his behavior on Ober and
the current state of Planet Raza, he is
undoubtedly the Demon Lord the
Captain spoke of.

He is indeed the Demon Lord
Asmodeus―the one recorded by the
Federation and worshipped by the Ober
since ancient times. And most likely...
He is a being who was\nsummoned by either Givel or\nEve.
Eek!?
Huh? Lavarnia, another\ncommunication! This time it's\nfrom the Stardust Bazaar.
From the Bazaar? I wonder\nwhat's going on.

Since realizing he was alive, he
had subjected his own body to
countless medical
examinations.
Yet, viewed objectively, such\nactions were riddled with\ncontradiction.
His body, mind, and abilities\nwere identical in every detail to\nwhat he remembered.
The more he confirmed his\ndeath, the more his life was\nvalidated.
The only discrepancies were\nthe clear memory that he\nshould not be alive,
and the memory of those who\nhad brought his life to an end―

The events etched into the
end of his memories―of a
half-life spent seeking a home
he no longer knew―
now drove his renewed\nexistence toward revenge and\nconquest.
Silvarant. Van Astral.
And...
Muah.

I remember them as if they
were right here... those sewer
rats who dared barge into my
laboratory...
...The memory of Muah, who\ndestroyed me―
And those kin of the former\nalien races.
Everything this world did to my\nlife has called my soul back\nonce more.
Evelysse.
My form is that of the one who\nawaits you at the end of your\njourney.
If you find that cursed, then\nyou would do well to be\ncautious.
Lady Lavarnia: No, this can't\nbe happening! ...What on earth\nwas the security force doing?!
What's all this? What\nhappened?

Lady Lavarnia: ...I'm right in the
middle of the front line
between Ober and Raza... Yes,
Heath is with me...

Lady Lavarnia: What, Papa... I'll
go help... Right, yes, I
understand... Please be
careful...
Lady Lavarnia. What exactly is\ngoing on...?

Lady Lavarnia: ...The Gem
mining asteroid belt within the
Stardust Bazaar territory has
been captured by Raza's army.
What?!

Lady Lavarnia: ...It's the largest deposit
on the outer edge of the Bazaar. Most
of the goods we've been smuggling
were diverted from there...

Has Raza's army finally lost it after
losing to the Phantoms over and over?!
Making an enemy of the Bazaar is way
worse than just a war!

Lady Lavarnia: I heard several
other small mines owned by
Bazaar citizens have also been
hit.

Lady Lavarnia: Apparently, a
fleet suddenly appeared out of
nowhere, and they were too
slow to react...
A fleet appearing out of\nnowhere... Could it be...!

Most likely. Many black
warships have been spotted.
The Bazaar is being attacked
by Ober's Phantom fleet...!
What the hell is going on...!
...It's probable that the upper\nechelons of Raza and Ober are\nconspiring.

Otherwise, there's no way the Raza
army―who shouldn't be able to predict
the appearance of Phantoms―could
spare the forces necessary to invade
the Bazaar.
Captain. I believe we should\nreturn to the Stardust Bazaar.
We should regroup with Rekoro\nand use our full capabilities to\nassess the situation.
Huh? What's all that noise in\nthe hallway...
Hold it right there!! Who said\nyou could just wander around?!\nGet back where you belong!!
Stop right there! What is your\nobjective!
Get back to the infirmary! Take\none more step forward and I\ncan't guarantee your life!

Well, well... it seems you don't
know your place. You're gravely
mistaken if you think we won't
kill you.
...Ober is.
Huh?
What Ober sought from the\nGate of Urza was the\nresurrection of Asmodeus.
...What are you talking about?
You know of it, do you not?\nThe power of the Gate of Urza.

Among the people of Ober,
there were those who lived for
hundreds, even thousands of
years.

Some of them came from a
space known as the Demon
Realm, and they knew
Asmodeus as he once was.

They worshipped the existence
of the Demon King, who ruled
them with absolute power, as
an absolute god.
Captain! It's dangerous! Get\nback!
I granted the wish of the Ober\npeople.

Until then, I had only
summoned Phantom; it was my
first summoning from the
Sparkling Stars.
From the Sparkling Stars...?

I know nothing of what
occurred between my defeat
by Asmodeus and my capture
by you.

Therefore, while I can
speculate on Evelysse's
current objective, I do not
know the exact details.
However... I can tell you what\nEvelysse once desired.\nEspecially to a human like you.
...Tell me, are you prepared to\ndo whatever it takes to stop\nEvelysse?
Stop Eve? What are you\ntalking about?

If Evelysse's goals haven't changed
since I last knew them, they should
align perfectly with the true objective
of Raza's army.

I had no such intention myself,
but for Ober, Asmodeus was
simply one means of assisting
Raza in achieving that goal.
...Get to the point. I have no\nidea what you're talking about.
Very well, I shall be blunt.

To my knowledge, the goal of
both Evelysse and Raza's army
is the destruction of Planet
Raza.
By using the Gate of Urza... or\nwhat you call the Urza System.
D-don't be ridiculous!
There is no way Eve―the great\nEve―would ever consider\ndestroying a planet!
Smuggling Gems... using the\nUrza System... to destroy\nRaza...
I see. "Destroying Raza," huh?\nA fitting choice of words.
Mastima... what do you mean?

Evelysse has always been
obsessed with the "natural
state" of how a planet should
be.
To Evelysse, the planet Raza\nmust be a far cry from that\nideal state.

...You mean she intends to use Gems to
"restore" the entire planet of
Raza―which was once Earth―to its
original form?
What!?
No way! If she does that, what\nhappens to the people living on\nRaza now!?
Who knows. If all goes well,\nperhaps they will simply remain\natop the restored Earth.

Even if the people of Raza survived, it's
obvious that doing something like that
would throw the whole world into
absolute chaos!!
That's beyond catastrophic!
Stop lying! There's no way Eve\nwould ever think of doing\nsomething like that!!

I am merely speaking of what I
know. Whether that is
Evelysse's true intention now, I
cannot say.

However, there have always
been those in Raza who
desired a return to the "Earth"
as it should have been,
And Ober, who wished to seize\ncontrol of the Azurite system,\nhad allies among them.
...Even so, Ober was never one\nto keep things organized.

With the appearance of
Asmodeus and the Phantom
fleet, the Raza army's
disadvantage became absolute.

Or rather, it would be more accurate to say
they walked right into it. Faced with an invasion
of monsters that cannot be reasoned with, it is
fair to say that current Raza is on the brink of
despair.
...Current Raza does not have\nthe power to simply flee into\nouter space.

In such a time, if one were to
spread the word that a "New
World" could be opened using
the Urza System...
But! There's no way hundreds\nof millions, billions of people in\nRaza would want that!

No... but... when a planet is
gripped by a "premonition of
ruin"... it is difficult to say for
certain how they will react.
I have... at least once,\nwitnessed such a case with my\nown eyes...
No way...!
...The current actions of the\nRaza Space Force support this\ntheory.

After receiving the information
regarding the invasion of
Stardust Bazaar, I contacted
Rekoro,
and discovered that illogical\nretreat orders have been\nissued across several fronts.

Even in sectors where they
hold a numerical advantage,
there are retreats on a scale
that collapses the entire line.
This is far from normal\nbehavior, and it appears many\nships have been sunk.

You mean the chain of
command isn't working? Don't
tell me the Phantoms broke it
that badly...
I find it unlikely they could\nhave penetrated that deeply in\nsuch a short time.
As Givel said, it's more natural\nto assume Raza is acting\naccording to some strategy.

But if they are driven by this
"premonition of doom" Mista
Henri mentioned... then we
have a real problem.

Dammit!! What are we
supposed to do... If ships are
